title: Playing in the desert for Blazing Saddles with Count Basie
summary: Callender and Willard talk about the brief big band scene shot in the Mojave, with wind and sand, and the long waits on film sets.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: I see. Okay, we'll look for that. I remember that brief shock in Blazing Saddles when suddenly you're on the screen a minute with Count Basie.
With Count Basie. Well, that was fun.
You showed up first, because you were standing up. It was easy to see you immediately.
Yeah.
I know there were some others... Everybody was from here, wasn't it? It was all L.A. musicians.
Well, mostly L.A. musicians, except I think Freddie Green... Was Freddie Green there? I'm not sure.
I can't remember. But it was so quick! I mean, you couldn't really look at the whole band. That quick desert shot, a marvelous...
Well, you know, the wind was blowing so hard that day, if you really get a second look at it...
[END OF SIDE ON ORIGINAL REEL]
You were talking about Blazing Saddles.
Yeah, and I was going to say that if you look close, you can see that I was hanging on to the bass,
Red Callender (Pt.2) - 44
because you know how the wind blows in the desert at times! The wind was so strong that day until it almost blew all of us off of the stand.
That meant the sand was blowing then. Right?
The sand and the wind.
Oh, it must have been awful.
So it might have looked like fun, but it was horrible.
Whereabouts in the desert was it shot?
Way out...past Lancaster, way out in... I guess when you go out Highway 14, off to the East, I guess...
That's the Mojave, isn't it.

Mojave. In the Mojave Desert, yeah. Well, somewhere in there they had found a location that would look good for the horses riding off, and all the other BS that goes with it, and they set up a bandstand there. You know, those things look like fun, but actually making pictures can be miserable, because you can be out there all day long and you might do nothing for six hours, and all of a sudden they're ready for you.
Well, I didn't mean to imply that I thought you had fun, because I didn't know. But I mean, it
Red Callender (Pt.2) - 45
was lots of fun in the picture all of a sudden to see a big band in the middle of the desert. I was just sorry it was so fast.

Oh, I don't want to make... Don't mistake me. It's all fun, you know. I love every second of all of it. But some of it you can have...it can be fun, and still be a little miserable. You know what I mean? It's fun just being there with all these people you love, you know? To me that's fun, being around capable musicians who can play. That's heaven. And you get paid for it, too! So I might bitch a little, but that's one of the pleasures of being a musician.
So could we stop for now?
